fixes.explanation: Jesus says the Father granted Him authority over all people “…so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.” That's the gift the verse names. It's a good one, baker. Eternal life is what Jesus gives.

Jesus doesn't talk about age here, friend. He says eternal life is “…that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.” It's about knowing God and Jesus Christ. Nobody is checking birthdays in verse 3.
I can see why a journey would come to mind. But Jesus says He accomplished “…the work You gave Me to do.” The word is work, not journey. Journey just isn't in the verse.

Jesus asks the Father, “…glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” Look at that word "had." He isn't asking for something brand new, friend. He's asking for the glory He had with the Father before the world existed.

Nothing about being scattered shows up in this verse. Jesus says of the disciples, “They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.” That's what they knew with certainty. Scattering isn't part of it.

Jesus says, “I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.” He isn't asking for them to be taken out of the world. His request is that the Father keep them from the evil one.
Jesus says, “Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.” He is asking the Father to sanctify them by the truth. And He says the Father's word is truth.

Jesus says, “I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message…” The prayer reaches past the disciples to people who believe through their message. That's a wide circle, friend, and Jesus prays for it.

It's in there, friend. Jesus says, “…so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.” So He prays that the world may know about the Father's love for them too.

Jesus says the Father gave Him glory “…because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.” So He places the Father's love for Him before the foundation of the world, not at His coming into it. That's the part to hold onto, baker.
